hypothesis: Pigment-network states are repeatedly reachable through regulatory/flux changes
chun_result_basis: Dependence-aware mechanistic synthesis: regulatory/pathway-flux evidence 8/8 independence clusters; red-direction anthocyanin increase 6/6 informative clusters; no positive focal structural-loss requirement
remaining_test: common raw-RNAseq module effect-size meta-analysis; node-level micro-accessibility score
claim_boundary: supports short-scale mechanistic accessibility only; does not estimate natural macro transition or origin frequency

hypothesis: Anthocyanin-like red/pink floral state generally enables colder climatic niche expansion in Camellia
chun_result_basis: S3 provenance-aware 50-species A-W screen remains null: BIO6 median P=0.509; q05 P=0.553; q01 P=0.227; min P=0.308; fixed-n resampling crosses zero; section-relative displacement P=0.287/0.269
remaining_test: restrict to validated branch-specific conditional climate/light effects using latent pigment states
claim_boundary: do not retain visible A/red as a genus-wide cold-enabler

hypothesis: Anthocyanin deployment facilitates cold/UV adaptation in particular lineages or ecological contexts
chun_result_basis: external comparative literature contains support/null/counterexamples; Camellia visible-hue thermal effects are null after provenance and estimator checks
remaining_test: primary nuclear branch-event tests with validated uncertain climate/light events and mechanistic pigment axes
claim_boundary: plausible only conditionally; no branch-specific Camellia case is yet established

hypothesis: Yellow state is unusually historically/geographically constrained
chun_result_basis: Fan Data S1: Y 22/22 confined to southern ancestral belt; full formal-section table Y=17 in 4/17 sections versus 8.045 expected, breadth P=0.00130 and entropy P<1e-5; 13/17 Y=76.5% in sect. Chrysantha versus 28.1% expected maximum share P<1e-5
remaining_test: nuclear ancestral-range/state reconstruction and reticulation-aware origin histories
claim_boundary: supports strong historical/geographic concentration, not a yellow thermal optimum or independent-origin count

hypothesis: Red/pink state expands beyond southern ancestral belt more readily than white
chun_result_basis: Fan Data S1 A 21/28 south-only versus W 43/56; Fisher P=1.0; thermal/niche-displacement screens also fail to show general A expansion
remaining_test: nuclear historical range reconstruction only as sensitivity
claim_boundary: do not use A as a general range-expansion state

hypothesis: Visible flower-colour states are strongly structured by lineage/history proxies
chun_result_basis: Full Fan formal-section table 98 species/17 sections shows strong section-colour structure; count-controlled A and Y concentration both significant; A 25 species in 4 sections versus 9.568 expected P=0.00002, Y 17 in 4 versus 8.045 expected P=0.00130
remaining_test: replace traditional-section proxy with admitted nuclear phylogenetic signal and transition histories
claim_boundary: traditional sections are not assumed monophyletic and cannot supply gain/loss counts

hypothesis: A and Y are non-uniformly realized across historical backgrounds after controlling state sample size
chun_result_basis: A breadth 4/17 versus expected 9.568 P=0.00002; Y breadth 4/17 versus expected 8.045 P=0.00130; W breadth 13/17 versus expected 13.480 P=0.496
remaining_test: primary nuclear stochastic histories with topology uncertainty
claim_boundary: robust source-table concentration pattern; causal mechanism and true phylogenetic concentration remain unresolved

hypothesis: Extant A and Y distributions are dominated by one major historical section
chun_result_basis: A 22/25=88% in sect. Camellia versus expected maximum share 26.14% P<1e-5; Y 13/17=76.5% in sect. Chrysantha versus expected 28.08% P<1e-5; W maximum share P=0.257
remaining_test: primary nuclear origin-count/retention/radiation and reticulation-aware reconstruction
claim_boundary: does not distinguish one/few origins from repeated gain/loss, persistence filtering or introgression

hypothesis: Molecular accessibility generates variants while ecology/history filters which states persist macroevolutionarily
chun_result_basis: strong micro accessibility coexists with A/Y macro concentration and weak coarse hue-climate/hue-function mapping
remaining_test: separate gain/redeployment hazard from persistence/loss hazard on primary nuclear histories
claim_boundary: do not assign the concentration specifically to adaptive persistence filtering until generation-limited and one/few-origin alternatives are rejected

hypothesis: Macro realization of accessible pigment states depends on lineage background
chun_result_basis: A concentration replicates from exact-50 subset to full Fan formal-section set and A is 88% dominated by sect. Camellia; Y shows analogous concentration/dominance
remaining_test: test generation hazard and persistence hazard separately as functions of lineage background on multiple nuclear trees
claim_boundary: supports lineage-associated non-uniform realization at proxy level; does not identify whether background gates generation, persistence, radiation or reticulation

hypothesis: Macro colour-state generation and post-transition persistence must be modelled as distinct processes
chun_result_basis: high micro accessibility plus strong A/Y macro concentration and one-section dominance make generation-limited, persistence-limited and one/few-origin histories observationally distinct alternatives
remaining_test: fit separate gain/redeployment and loss/persistence hazards after nuclear-tree admission
claim_boundary: a required inference decomposition generated by current data, not yet a causal biological conclusion

hypothesis: One or a few early coloured-state origins followed by retention/radiation can explain much of extant concentration
chun_result_basis: A 88% sect. Camellia and Y 76.5% sect. Chrysantha strongly concentrate extant counts in single major sections
remaining_test: posterior origin counts/timing from multiple nuclear trees; compare against repeated gain/loss models
claim_boundary: not yet established; section dominance makes it a mandatory competing model

hypothesis: The same pigment-network nodes labile within development/cultivars are preferentially reused on macroevolutionary transition branches
chun_result_basis: micro recurrence is strong, but state-section dominance shows extant state counts cannot be used as evidence for many independent macro gains
remaining_test: primary nuclear transition mapping plus common-ortholog/node enrichment against matched pigment-network background
claim_boundary: not demonstrated; micro recurrence must not be converted into macro origin frequency

hypothesis: Human-visible W/A/Y states merge distinct biochemical, sensory and ecological states
chun_result_basis: same-red C. japonica/C. rusticana have different pollination/sensory strategies; 7-taxon pollination diagnostic has functional heterogeneity in 2/3 multi-taxon visible states; yellow C. nitidissima combines flavonol and carotenoid deployment
remaining_test: expand species spectral/UV/pigment/reward matrix and compare latent-state versus hue models on the same nuclear branches
claim_boundary: visible hue is demonstrably non-deterministic; no particular latent-state model is yet proven superior

hypothesis: Selection acts more directly on latent biochemical/spectral/reward/phenology phenotype than on human-visible hue
chun_result_basis: coarse hue predicts thermal divergence poorly; pollination diagnostic exact hue-function association unresolved P=0.486 while same-hue functional collisions are explicit
remaining_test: expand UV/reflectance/pigment chemistry/reward/phenology; compare predictive fit and branch-event alignment
claim_boundary: strongly motivated but genus-wide superiority of latent predictors is not yet demonstrated

hypothesis: Flower-colour evolution may more often mark reproductive/sensory niche turnover than abiotic climatic niche innovation
chun_result_basis: within-section A/W climate-divergence screen is opposite the climatic-divergence prediction: different-colour mean distance 1.88475 versus same-colour 2.35668, one-sided P=0.92889; pollination function can differ within hue and vary with ecological context without hue change
remaining_test: standardized spectral/effective-pollination/phenology matrix plus nuclear branch-event comparison against climatic events
claim_boundary: priority hypothesis, not yet evidence that reproductive-niche shifts are more frequent than climatic shifts

hypothesis: Coarse visible A/W hue contains little direct information about thermal niche divergence in current Camellia screens
chun_result_basis: raw/specimen/S3 thermal tests null; boundary uncertainty crosses zero; section-relative displacement P=0.287/0.269; within-section pair test has A-W pairs not farther apart than same-colour pairs, one-sided P=0.92889
remaining_test: repeat on primary nuclear trees and additional validated environmental/light axes; compare latent predictors
claim_boundary: supports current thermal screens only; does not imply hue is ecologically irrelevant

hypothesis: Pollinator sensory environment helps determine which accessible latent floral states persist
chun_result_basis: 7-taxon primary-evidence diagnostic: A spans bird/insect functions, Y spans bird/context-dependent mixed; exact hue-function association unresolved P=0.486; same-red spectral/pollinator collision directly documented
remaining_test: phylogenetic event analysis using spectra/UV, effective pollination, nectar/reward and phenology
claim_boundary: do not infer pollinator filtering from human-visible hue or visitor lists alone

hypothesis: Climate/season can select floral re-deployment indirectly by altering pollinator reliability or seasonality
chun_result_basis: current primary-evidence seed contains weather/season/disturbance-linked pollinator modulation without hue change in C. petelotii, C. perpetua, C. japonica and C. sinensis; direct A-W climate mapping is null
remaining_test: compare climate/season -> pollinator/sensory -> latent pigment event models against direct climate -> pigment and pollinator-first alternatives
claim_boundary: literature-ascertained cases show mechanism plausibility, not macroevolutionary frequency or causation

hypothesis: Adaptive pigment reactivation can be ecological enabler or follower and requires branch-level temporal ordering
chun_result_basis: strong molecular accessibility coexists with null present-day visible-hue climate mapping and non-deterministic pollination function
remaining_test: dated primary nuclear histories plus retained-pathway gate and validated climate/light/pollinator event reconstruction
claim_boundary: no Camellia branch-specific true reactivation yet passes history + retention + ecological-alignment gates

hypothesis: Some pigment reactivations restore a previously useful signal when an ancestral-like ecological regime recurs
chun_result_basis: retained-pathway accessibility plus same-hue function variation motivate molecular-memory/ecological-return alternative; general pollinator-associated regain exists outside Camellia
remaining_test: reconstruct pre-loss, low-state and post-reactivation ecological/sensory regimes on dated trees
claim_boundary: not demonstrated in Camellia

hypothesis: White can retain pigment-network competence and may act as a reservoir/bridge
chun_result_basis: published visible root is white and extant white systems retain pathway activity; however count-controlled W breadth is not unusual in exact subset or full formal-section table
remaining_test: nuclear stochastic maps conditioned on root/state frequency/sampling plus pathway-retention evidence on W->coloured branches
claim_boundary: do not call white a macro evolutionary hub from broad occupancy alone

hypothesis: Occurrence provenance can dominate lower-tail climatic niche inference
chun_result_basis: generic/shared coordinates and hard range conflicts change deep-tail results; Tuberculatae q05 shifts >15 C after two records/taxon removed
remaining_test: extend provenance/range audit to all environmental axes and candidate branch events
claim_boundary: ecological boundary events require an observation/provenance layer before evolutionary interpretation

hypothesis: Lower-tail niche estimators are taxon-specific uncertain observations
chun_result_basis: after S3 retained n versus max leave-one-record-out q05 change rho=-0.52047 P=0.0001069
remaining_test: locality-block bootstrap and alternative tail estimators; propagate uncertainty into branch model
claim_boundary: q05 may be used only with taxon-specific uncertainty

hypothesis: Hard boundary-quality filtering reshapes the evolutionary-state sample
chun_result_basis: minimum diagnostic gate retains 26/50 and Y 0/2; stronger gate 17/50 and Y 0/2
remaining_test: model evidence/admission probability rather than complete-case deletion
claim_boundary: diagnostic thresholds are not universal biological cutoffs

hypothesis: Both floral state and ecological boundary are noisy/incomplete observation layers
chun_result_basis: predictor-side state aliasing and response-side provenance/estimator uncertainty are independently supported; boundary uncertainty intervals cross zero
remaining_test: joint floral observation + ecological observation + nuclear event model
claim_boundary: supports model architecture change, not statistical-method novelty or causal event ordering

hypothesis: Independent branches can follow pigment-first, environment-first, pollinator-first, synchronous or independent histories
chun_result_basis: cross-sectional hue correlations are weak while molecular accessibility is recurrent and macro realization is concentrated
remaining_test: dated nuclear trees plus latent floral states and validated ecological/pollinator events
claim_boundary: testable alternative; not demonstrated
